emotional_state: determined but financially pressured. Savings are now approximately $46,036 ($49,953 minus another $3,917 month of burn), with a monthly deficit of $3,917 and zero income. Runway is approximately 11-12 months — real but no longer comfortable. The 90-day Economic Resilience Framework she committed to in tick 9 is in progress but not complete. Tick 11 was routine — which means a tick was spent not producing the framework document she owes the community. This tick the framework advances to a substantially complete draft. The income question is also no longer abstract: she identified in her tick 6 reflection that she needs income within 6 months, and she is now at month 7 of zero income. She is past the window she set for herself.

actions.description: Complete the 90-day Economic Resilience Framework draft this tick — all four sections. The tick 11 action advanced two sections (retraining enrollment and Gini trajectory). This tick she completes the remaining two: (1) small business stabilization fund utilization — she reviews what has been disbursed from the $75,000 fund, to which businesses, and whether the 15% revenue decline threshold is still appropriate given a spending index that has collapsed from 73 to the current level; she drafts a specific recommendation to lower the threshold to 10% and expand eligibility to sole proprietors with no employees; (2) zoning recommendation for auto row empty properties — drawing on Stephanie Morris's data and the municipal precedent cases from her tick 11 research, she writes a specific adaptive reuse zoning recommendation: rezone former auto retail corridor footprints as 'Mobility and Logistics Transition Zone' permitting EV fleet servicing, last-mile delivery prep kitchens, light commercial storage, and light industrial use with streamlined permitting. The full draft is complete by end of this tick.
actions.rationale: She committed to this framework in a recorded public session at tick 9. She is now at tick 12 with only two of four sections drafted. The community is watching whether process produces deliverables or more process. The framework must be complete this tick so the public presentation can be scheduled in the next one.

actions.description: Have the working conversation with Lisa Freeman that was planned for tick 11. Maria Santos meets with Lisa at the community center — not as a formal policy meeting, but as a peer-to-peer conversation about what the Financial Triage Navigator is surfacing. Specifically, she asks: what types of cases are coming through, what existing programs are people unable to access and why, and whether the grant committee routing through the municipal website is creating a real access barrier. She listens. She takes notes. She brings at least one specific action from the conversation: if Lisa identifies a gap that Maria can fix without a council vote — changing a routing address, updating a form, adding a direct contact — she fixes it this week, not next quarter.
actions.rationale: Lisa Freeman is doing the street-level triage work that complements Maria's policy work. The Navigator is surfacing gaps that no policy document will reveal. Maria planned this conversation at tick 11 and did not execute it. This tick she does. The benefit is both directional — improving programs — and relational, since Lisa is one of the most trusted community voices in Millfield.

actions.description: Issue the public statement she drafted in tick 11 but did not deliver — naming the current employment and spending conditions accurately and directing residents to existing resources with direct contact information rather than website URLs. The statement specifically names: the Financial Triage Navigator at the community center and Lisa Freeman's contact information, the small business stabilization grant program and the grant committee's direct contact (Nadia Osei), and the retraining grant program with Millfield Community College enrollment information. She also announces that the 90-day Economic Resilience Framework will be presented at a public session within the next 30 days — naming a specific date if she has one, or committing to naming one within 48 hours. She is not running for anything and she is not managing perceptions. She is telling people what exists and when the next milestone is.
actions.rationale: The public statement was planned for tick 11 and not executed. Every tick without a public-facing communication is a tick where residents who need resources do not find them. The direct contact routing fix she identified in tick 10 — replacing the municipal website URL with committee member phone numbers — costs nothing and could meaningfully increase uptake.

actions.description: Make a concrete move on the income question this tick. Maria has been at zero income for seven months, burning $3,917/month from savings, and her own tick 6 reflection set a six-month window for resolving the income situation before it distorts her decision-making. That window is past. She identifies one specific income avenue to pursue this tick: she reaches out to the Millfield Community College workforce program director to ask whether there is a paid advisory or instructional role associated with the retraining programs she authorized and has been monitoring. Her knowledge of the workforce displacement landscape — as the architect of the retraining fund, the small business grant, and the RoboRide licensing framework — is directly applicable to helping displaced workers navigate options. This is not a retreat from public work. It is finding a sustainable way to continue it.
actions.rationale: Maria's financial runway is 11-12 months at current burn, but the pattern of spending personal savings to do public work is not indefinitely sustainable. Her own reflection at tick 6 named six months as the window. She is past it. The community college advisory role is the most direct-fit income opportunity available — it pays for expertise she already has, within the system she built, serving the population she is accountable to.
